pages.text:
ATYPICAL STIFF PERSON SYNDROME WITH ANTI-IGLON5
ANTIBODIES: A CASE REPORT
Chiara Castellano1, Margherita Bellucci 1, Francesco Germano 1, Chiara
Gemelli2, Lucio Marinelli 1, Anastasia Lechiara 2, Angelo Schenone 1,
Diego Franciotta3, Luana Benedetti 2
1University of Genoa, DINOGMI, Genoa, Italy; 2IRCCS Hospital Policlinico
S. Martino, Genoa, Italy; 3IRCCS Mondino Foundation, Neuroimmunology
Laboratory, Pavia, Italy
Stiff Person Syndrome (SPS) and IgLON5 disease are two apparently
unrelated rare neuroimmunological disorders. The mean features of SPS
are rigidity and painful spasms while the mean features of IgLON5 dis-
ease are parasomnias, bulbar symptoms, cognitive impairment, respira-
tory failure and IgLON5 antibodies.
Herein we report a case of neuromuscular hyperexcitability overlap-
ping with Stiff Person Syndrome associated with anti-IgLON5 anti-
bodies positivity.
A 82-year-old man presented to visit with muscular fasciculations and
cramps, together with diffuse limb stiffness and frequent falls. Electro-
diagnostic studies (EDX) and laboratory tests with an antibody panel
were performed.
EDX showed signs of neuromuscular hyperexcitability. Anti-IgLON5
antibodies were positive on both serum and CSF. Brain MRI, brain
PET and body CT/PET were uninformative.
Treatment with IV corti costeroids, followed by oral benzodiazepines
prompted functional recovery, whichpersisted at a four-months follow-up.
This case demonstrates a unique overlap between neuromuscular
hyperexcitability and Stiff Person Syndrome with a so far never
reported seropositivity for anti-IgLON5 antibodies.
Future evaluations are necessary to confirm whether such findings
could lead to a broadening of the SPS clinical and laboratory features.
